node.title: Re: How is the default "Input Record Separator" set?
node.author: Marshall
node.doctext:
I am also a Windows user.
The text I/O layers will take out and what Perl sees is just .
So \n for input is just one character, even on Windows.
For output, Windows will emit for an \n. On Unix, just a .

I am curious as to why you think that something has changed?
Some code would be very helpful!

Update: [Haukex] replied while I was writing this. I agree with what he said. Unless you are using binmode, you will never see a . I am not even sure that you can even set $/ to CRLF. Please show some code where you think that you did that.
